task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-06-19, in the area of play-type labeling and data quality):
Opponent next-possession PPP after you run play X is large enough to drive AVOID labels; own-sequence lags similarly matter.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

methodological_questions: effect of next-possession PPP on labeling

historical_evidence.finding: After the opponent runs play type X, the next offensive play Y scores above Y's unconditional H2 baseline, and every PT has a defensive aftershock. Observed aftershock values replicated across all games and playoffs.
Play-type PPP differences are inflated by foul leakage for OTHER and lowered for DRIVE; labeling artifact found.

failed_approaches.what_failed: assessment of PPP differences without accounting for foul leakage
analysis limited by small sample for some play types

evidence_establishes: Opponent play type X influences next possession PPP and defensive aftershock exists; PPP measurement can be biased by fouls.
evidence_does_not_establish: Magnitude of PPP effect sufficient to drive AVOID labeling thresholds; effects of own-sequence lags on labeling; generalization to all play types.
own_inferences: PPP effects are real and measurable but must be controlled for fouls; labeling may be biased by PPP magnitude.
uncertainties: Magnitude of PPP effect relative to labeling thresholds; availability of sufficient data across all seasons; potential confounding by score margin and period.

historical_effect.explanation: Prior work demonstrates both a genuine opponent PPP effect and a labeling bias due to fouls, indicating the question is testable but requires design adjustments.

blocking_constraints.text: PPP measurement may be inflated by foul leakage.
Game context (score margin, period) may confound PPP effects.
AVOID labeling may be mis-specified if PPP thresholds are inaccurate.
Some play types have limited sample sizes.
Selection bias in play-type labeling could affect estimates.

prior_work.summary: Earlier studies confirm that opponent play type influences next-possession PPP and highlight PPP measurement bias from fouls, but they do not fully address the effect size needed for AVOID labeling or own-sequence lag effects.

risks.text: PPP measurement may be inflated by foul leakage.
Score margin and period may confound PPP effect estimates.
AVOID labeling may be mis-specified if PPP thresholds are inaccurate.
Limited sample for rare play types may reduce power.
Selection bias in play-type labeling may distort the analysis.
Testing many play types increases false-positive risk.

design.estimand: Difference in PPP for next possession following opponent play type X versus baseline PPP of that play type
design.sample: All possessions from 2022-23 to 2025-26 seasons, including playoffs, with sufficient counts per play type
design.power: 80% to detect an effect size of 0.02 points per possession at alpha=0.05 after FDR adjustment
design.controls: Opponent score margin, period, foul count, and defensive matchup minutes
design.falsification: Test the same estimand using random play types not expected to influence PPP
design.multiplicity: Apply Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction across play types
design.decision_rule: Reject null if adjusted p<0.05; otherwise fail to reject
